text:
F-0p2y (Innsbruck, ULB Tirol, Frg. D3): source-assisted reading, made with the image-only first reading and the Venice 1509 print of the Liber novem iudicum (Warburg facsimile) in hand. Lines reread on crops of the images by a research reader: 01_r (canvas 0) lines 1-9; 02_r (canvas 2) lines 1-10; 02_v (canvas 3) lines 1-13, some of them after seeing the print. 01_v (canvas 1) was not reread; its two rubrics below were read by two blind readers. Readings the blind readers did not confirm are marked (?) or [words uncertain]. All other lines rest on the first reading only. Expansions in parentheses; [..] lost or unread; (?) uncertain; red = rubric in red. Boxes are native pixels.

6. oriens ip(su)m(?) agr(orum) incolas eor(um)q(ue) si(gnifica)t(i)o(n)e(m) accipiat
7. A quarto ite(m) agr(orum) status et qualitas req(ui)rat(ur). Septimu(m) na(m)-

(Line 1: the first word has a large initial of C or T form; reading of the word uncertain. "p(ro)p(r)iis manib(us)" fits both blind readers.)

10. Rursu(m) si de thesauro nulla sit ambiguitas relicta: q(ua)lit(a)s ip(s)ius et n(atur)a [..]
(The two-line rubric was read by the research reader as "de pecunia reposita fratr[..]" / "[..]ntibus Aomar"; two blind readers did not confirm it.)
